description: Receive inserts, updates and deletes from the Supabase tables you choose, one document per row. Rows that existed before you set it up are not loaded.
opening: Supabase sends each insert, update and delete on the tables you choose to HydraDB, through Database Webhooks you add in Supabase. Each row is one document, with one searchable line per content column. HydraDB needs no Supabase credentials and does not read your database.

Rows that existed before you added the webhooks do not come across. Row-level security is not imported, so every row is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Deleting a row in Supabase asks HydraDB to remove its document, which can stay if the row is still being indexed or a newer change has replaced it. Changes sent while the connector is paused are lost.

connect.text: A row is identified by its table name and primary key only. If two Supabase projects or connectors send a table with the same name to the same collection, rows with the same key overwrite each other. Send them to separate collections.

notes: Supabase row-level security policies are not reproduced.

connect.auth: HydraDB stores no Supabase credentials. Each Supabase webhook sends its changes with a HydraDB API key and the connector id in its headers.

credentials.name: tables
credentials.text: The tables to accept, schema-qualified, one per line, for example `public.orders`. A change for any other table is refused.

steps.title: List your tables
steps.text: Create the Supabase connector in HydraDB and list the tables you want as `tables`, schema-qualified. A query over `information_schema.tables` can produce the list. An entry in a system schema, or an invalid entry, is rejected.

steps.title: Describe each table, if needed
steps.text: Through the API, you can send a schema for a table in `provider_metadata.schema` when you add it. A schema can name the primary key, the role of each column, a title template, the timestamp column and foreign keys. Without one, the primary key is `id` and the column rules under What gets synced apply.

steps.title: Add a webhook for each table
steps.text: In Supabase, add a Database Webhook on each table for `INSERT`, `UPDATE` and `DELETE` that sends a POST request to HydraDB's `/webhooks/supabase` endpoint.

steps.title: Set the webhook headers
steps.text: Set the `Authorization` header to `Bearer` followed by a HydraDB API key, and the `X-HydraDB-Connector` header to the connector id.

connect.account: One connector covers the tables you list in it.

sync.first_sync: Nothing is loaded when you connect. Only changes made after the webhooks exist arrive. To bring in an existing row, change it or send its change again.
sync.changes: Each insert or update arrives as it happens and updates the row's document. An insert with no content columns is skipped.
sync.edits: An update replaces the row's document. A primary-key change asks HydraDB to remove the document under the old key. An update that empties every content column asks HydraDB to remove the row's document under its current key and any replaced key. As with a delete, a document can stay if it is still being indexed or a newer change has replaced it.
sync.deletes: A delete asks HydraDB to remove the row's document. The document can stay if the row is still being indexed when the delete arrives, or a newer change has already replaced it.
notes: While the connector is paused, every change, deletes included, is refused, and Supabase does not send it again.
A change for a table you did not list is refused with an error, so a misconfigured webhook is visible.
Changes count against HydraDB's ingestion rate limit. A bulk update sends one request per row.

documents.name: Rows
documents.one_document: One row of a listed table, identified by its table and primary key.
documents.title: The table's title template with column values filled in. Without a template, the table name and the row's primary key.
documents.text: One `column: value` line per non-empty content column, sorted by column name. Nested JSON is written as compact JSON. Without a schema, `id` is the key, timestamp columns, status columns and columns ending in `_id` are kept out of the text, columns starting with `_` are ignored, and every other column is content. Column roles in a schema override these rules. The title is searchable too, so a title template can put a key or status value into searchable text.
documents.date: The value of the timestamp column named in the table's schema. Without one, the row has no date.

attributes.name: Content columns
attributes.text: Each content column's value, one line per column.

attributes.name: Timestamp column
attributes.text: The column the schema names as the timestamp. Its value is the result date. This date is not searchable as a separate field.

attributes.name: Foreign keys
attributes.text: Each foreign key named in the schema, when it has a value, links the row to the row it references. One declaration covers one column, so a key made of several columns cannot be linked. Not searchable.

attributes.name: table, row_key, updated_at
attributes.text: The table name, the row's key and its timestamp value.

example_searches: What do our orders rows say about delayed shipments?
Which support_tickets rows mention a refund?

connections: A row to each row its schema's foreign keys reference.
Each row is grouped under its table.
No links to items in other tools.
graph.people: No one is attached to a row as a person.
graph.from_text: The content columns of each row.

not_synced: Rows that existed before the webhooks were added.
Tables not listed in the connector. Their changes are refused.
Changes sent while the connector is paused.
Columns with the ignore role. Columns starting with `_` are ignored unless a schema gives them another role.
